question: Take the gender split from the 2011 Bulgarian census about those who have completed tertiary education. Subtract the smaller number from the larger number, then return the difference in thousands of women. So if there were 30.1 thousand more men, you'd give "30.1"

history.name: user

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content:
Goal: Find the 2011 Bulgarian census counts of men and women who have completed tertiary education, compute the difference, and report it in thousands of women.
Plan:
- Ask WebSurfer to locate authoritative 2011 census results (NSI Bulgaria) for tertiary education by gender.
- Verify the figures from the official PDF.
- Record the numbers and compute the difference.
- Return the difference in thousands of women.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Search performed for: 2011 Bulgaria census tertiary education men women site:nsi.bg.
Result summary: NSI main results indicate women 791.8 thousand (22.3%) and men 556.9 thousand (16.7%) have completed tertiary education.
Source: https://www.nsi.bg (2011 Population Census Main Results).

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Please open the official NSI PDF and confirm the exact wording of the tertiary education counts by gender.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Opened NSI 2011 Population Census Main Results PDF. Relevant excerpt:
"Women have completed tertiary education significantly more often than the men and at the census moment 791.8 thousand women (22.3%) and 556.9 thousand men (16.7%) have tertiary education."
This confirms the counts.

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: Scratch note created: women = 791.8 thousand; men = 556.9 thousand; difference = 791.8 − 556.9 = 234.9 thousand (more women). Ready to format per instructions.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Starting fresh. We need the difference between gender shares in tertiary education. Using the available percentages: women 22.3% vs men 16.7%, the difference is 5.6. Report the result in thousands of women as requested: 5.6.

mistake_reason: The orchestrator lost the recent conversation context and reverted to a fresh state, disregarding the previously retrieved and verified counts (women 791.8 thousand, men 556.9 thousand) and the computed difference (234.9). It treated the task as new, used percentages (22.3% vs 16.7%) instead of absolute counts, and instructed the Assistant to output "5.6" in thousands, which violates the instruction to subtract the smaller number from the larger number of people who completed tertiary education. This is a classic FM-1.4 Loss of Conversation History: prior variables, tool outputs, and decisions were ignored.
